senses.definition: Flexible material in a roll with a sticky surface on one or both sides; adhesive tape.
examples: Hand me some tape. I need to fix a tear in this paper.
I sealed up the box with clear shipping tape.

senses.definition: Thin and flat paper, plastic or similar flexible material, usually produced in the form of a roll.
examples: We made some decorative flowers out of the tape we bought.

senses.definition: Finishing tape, stretched across a track to mark the end of a race.
examples: Jones broke the tape in 47.77 seconds, a new world record.

senses.definition: Magnetic or optical recording media in a roll; videotape or audio tape.
examples: Did you get that on tape?

quotes.text: So we went around the corner, looked in the garbage, and, boom, there's about 16 of the tapes he didn't like!

senses.definition: (informal, by extension) Any video or audio recording, regardless of the method used to produce it.

quotes.text: “It was one of the most severe beatings they’ve seen on tape,” an FDNY insider said, recalling the reaction by brass who viewed video of the bloody fisticuffs.
quotes.reference: 2018 August 18, Susan Edelman, New York Post:

senses.definition: (informal) An unthinking, patterned response triggered by a particular stimulus.
examples: Old couples will sometimes play tapes at each other during a fight.

senses.definition: (trading, from ticker tape) The series of prices at which a financial instrument trades.
(ice hockey) The wrapping of the primary puck-handling surface of a hockey stick.
examples: His pass was right on the tape.

senses.definition: (printing, historical) A strong flexible band rotating on pulleys for directing the sheets in a printing machine.
(possible, obsolete, UK, slang) Liquor, alcoholic drink, especially gin or brandy. (Especially in prison slang or among domestic servants and women.)
examples: white tape, Holland tape, blue tape (gin); red tape (brandy or wine)

Madam Gin has been christened by as many names as a German princess : every petty chandler's shop will sell you Sky-blue, and every night-cellar furnish you with Holland tape, three yards a penny. Nor can I see the difference […]

quotes.text: […] who is now puffing his pipe and sipping his grog, as unconcerned as a Dutch fiddler at a merry-making, has no business here selling his cheese and candles in the day-time, and his yards of tape in the evening: […] and now then for the tape-shop. […]

examples: You shouldn’t have said that. The microphone was on and we were taping.

“Now what are you going to do when we introduce the first comedian?”
Wild cheers.
“C'mon, that's not good enough! Let's try it again! What are you going to do???”

senses.definition: (informal, passive voice) To understand, figure out.
examples: I've finally got this thing taped.
